question: what is the policy on withdrawing from a class after the deadline and does it affect my aid/satisfactory academic progress

body.answer:
After the published withdrawal deadline, a student may NOT withdraw from a course [3]. The deadline is on the [Academic Calendar](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/). The catalog describes a possible late administrative withdrawal under extraordinary circumstances: ordinarily apply before the semester ends; explain why standard withdrawal procedures could not be followed and identify the term. Typically, approval means W grades for all courses in that term, and ordinarily only one term per appeal. Documentation may include medical records, a death certificate, proof of required family caregiving, disaster-relocation documentation, or an employer’s dated relocation letter. The Provost or designee decides; the burden of proof is on the student [2, 5].

Withdrawing may affect financial aid and progress toward graduation [1]. For a withdrawal from any classes, Financial Aid recommends discussing the impact on your current aid package with its office [6, 10]. If withdrawing leaves you with fewer than 6 credits, federal aid should not be affected if you remain enrolled in 6 or more credits; NJ state aid requires full-time enrollment when fully disbursed [10]. Students who officially withdraw or leave school before 60% of the semester ends are subject to Title IV aid return rules; the amount is based on the percentage of the term attended, and repayment may be required [9].

SAP is reviewed annually after spring. Standards include completing at least 67% of attempted credits, undergraduate GPA of at least 2.0 or graduate GPA of 3.0, and staying within 150% of the program’s published length [7]. The pages do not determine your individual aid or SAP outcome.

Registrar: reg@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7695, D-224 [3]. Provost: provost@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7330 [2]. Financial Aid: finaid@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7549, E-210 [6, 7, 9, 10].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#dropping-or-withdrawing-from-a-course1) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#withdrawal-or-leave-of-absence-from-the-college) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/policies/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/policies/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/)

value.heading: What types of aid are available?
value.text: Financial aid available at Ramapo consists of grants, loans and work-study. Grants are awards that don’t have to be paid back, whereas loans must be paid back. value.heading: Student Placement Process
value.text: All federal work-study and student aide positions are posted on Handshake. Students are able to view all open positions and apply directly to the hiring units. The unit supervisor (or delegate) describes the position, responsibilities, etc. to student and makes a decision whether to offer the student the position. value.heading: What employment programs are available?
value.text: There are two major student employment programs with different requirements: a. Federal Work-Study (FWS) is a need-based financial aid award available to United States citizens and permanent resident aliens. Students apply and, if eligible, are awarded work-study that is based on individual financial need. FWS students may then earn up to the award specified by the Financial Aid Office during the academic year. b. The Student Assistant Program is funded as part of the College’s operating budget and is based on institutional guidelines. Students who are United States citizens, permanent resident aliens or on F-1 visas are eligible for this type of employment. Student aides are hired through program or project-based awards. These positions are generally ability-dependent (skilled), requiring a “fit” between position requirements and student abilities. Ability may refer to specialized knowledge, assignment familiarity, effective communication/interpersonal skills or willingness to comply with specific project and supervisory requirements.

value.heading: Are there other kinds of employment on campus?
value.text: Funding for student employees is occasionally available through faculty and administrators who are awarded grants by the state, federal government, foundations or private corporations. Students apply directly to these programs or supervisors for available positions. These positions could be posted on Handshake. Also the Campus Bookstore and Campus Dining Service offer positions to students on campus.

value.heading: Earnings Allowed
value.text: If a student is eligible for financial aid based on need, the Office of Financial Aid will allot a specific award of Federal Work-Study that indicates the maximum amount that can be earned during the fiscal year. Students who are not eligible for FWS awards, but have been approved for student aide positions, will be allowed to work within permitted hours up to the unit allocation. The supervisor must be aware that heavy summer use and work during semester breaks by student employees using their student aid budget might negatively affect the ability to meet unit needs during the academic year.

value.heading: Payment Plans Offered to Students
value.text: The College manages an in-house installment payment plan to assist students and parents in paying their term bill. value.heading: Parent Plus and Alternative Loans
value.text: During this unprecedented time, a Parent Plus Loan or an alternative loan may be able to assist you and your family in covering the costs to attend college. question: im a transfer student and i commute, how do i get a parking permit and where do i park

body.answer:
**Public Safety** handles permits and parking. Register at [Parking Permits](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/) [2, 3].

One page’s steps: “Enter Permit Type and click Continue”; complete Contact Information, click “Save/Update Person” and “Continue”; enter Vehicle Information and click “Continue”; review the request and click “Continue”; print or save the “Registration Filed” page with your request number. That page is verification, not the permit. Select “student” and the correct commuter status. New-student permits are available for pickup during New Student Check-In. [9]

The pages differ: another student FAQ instead directs applicants to https://ramapo.thepermitstore.com/ and gives a different process: enter Ramapo, choose Ramapo College of New Jersey, click Apply, agree to terms, sign in; complete personal information, select a permit, enter vehicle information, proceed to payment (dropdown should read “No Payment Necessary”), then Finish. It says to print a temporary permit from the account, display it until the permanent permit arrives by mail, then activate the permit online. [10]

For 2026–2027, the listed Fall/Spring permit is $250.00 and the Fall/Spring Commuter Parking Tax Charge is $16.58. Off-campus students are subject to 6.63% sales tax. [14, 11]

**Where to park:** The page says students may use C1, C2, or D lots as overflow if their assigned lot is full. It does not identify your assigned commuter lot. Commuters may not park overnight (2am–6am) without prior Public Safety authorization. [5]

For your assigned lot or which application process applies, contact Public Safety at parkingpermits@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7432. [9, 21]

question: do transfer students need to take all the gen ed / Intellectual Inquiry requirements again or do some get waived?

body.answer:
No—not necessarily. Transfer students may transfer in or be waived from some or all General Education requirements [3].

• NJ community college graduates with an A.A. or A.S. are waived from General Education requirements after submitting a final official transcript with the conferred degree. A.A.S. graduates are not eligible for a full waiver; courses are evaluated individually [8].
• Students transferring at least 48 credits from an accredited institution without a completed A.A. or A.S. degree are waived from some requirements [2]. For students with at least 48 credits, the listed waived keystone courses are First Year Seminar, Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Social Science Inquiry, and Studies in the Arts and Humanities. They must still fulfill Critical Reading and Writing 102, Quantitative Reasoning, and Scientific Reasoning, and take one course from two of Culture and Creativity, Values and Ethics, and Social Systems and Society [1].
• Transfer credits are generally considered for possible Gen Ed waivers only if accepted in the semester of matriculation [4]. The distribution requirement is two of those three categories [7].

Catalog transfer-equivalent courses listed are: HIST 100T TRANSFER GE HISTORY EQUIVALENT: Gen Ed 18-Historical Prspctve (GEHP); INTD 200T TRANSFER GE GLOBA AWR EQ: Gen Ed 18-Global Awareness (GEGA); INTD 201T TRANSFER GE CULT & CREAT EQ: Gen Ed 18-Culture & Creativity (GECC); INTD 203T TRANSFER GE VAL & ETH EQ: Gen Ed 18-Values and Ethics (GEVE); and INTD 280 TRANSFER ELECTIVE: VALUE & ETHICS: Gen Ed 18-Values and Ethics (GEVE). EDUC 211 STUDENT LITERACY CORPS: Gen Ed 18-Values and Ethics (GEVE) [11].

Office of the Provost can advise you on applicable waivers and remaining requirements during academic advisement [1]. Email provost@ramapo.edu or call (201) 684-7330. Admissions: admissions@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7300 [8].

question: how do i get a parking permit and how much does it cost

body.answer:
**How to apply:** Public Safety directs students to the online Parking Permit Registration portal [6, 9]. Its regulations say to ensure the parking fee is on your RCNJ student account, then visit the Parking Permits webpage [7]. Another page gives these steps: “Enter Permit Type and click Continue”; complete Contact Information, click “Save/Update Person” and “Continue”; enter Vehicle Information and “Continue”; review and “Continue”; then print or save the Registration Filed page as verification—not as the permit. Select the correct housing assignment or commuter status, and “student,” not “faculty/staff” [12].

The Orientation FAQ gives a different portal and process: log on to ThePermitStore.com; enter Ramapo as your destination, choose Ramapo College of New Jersey, click Apply, agree to terms, sign in, complete the four application steps (personal information, permit, vehicle, payment), then Finish. It says to print the temporary permit, display it on the dashboard until the permanent permit arrives, then activate the permit online [11]. The pages therefore give different portal instructions [6, 9, 11, 12].

New students pick up permits at New Student Check-In; returning residents at their on-campus mailbox; returning commuters at the Public Safety ID Office during weekday operating hours, or at the Main Desk after 3 pm by emailing to request another pickup time [7, 12]. Permit fee automatically appears on the term bill [1, 10]. Applications open mid-May for summer permits and early August for Fall/Spring permits; follow Public Safety messages for specific dates [10].

**Cost:** The 2026–2027 fee text includes “Spring-only Commuter Parking Tax Charge | $8.29,” “Spring-only Resident Parking Supplement | $25.00,” “Summer-only Parking Permit | $100.00,” and “Summer-only Commuter Parking Tax Charge | $6.63” [5]. It also has the truncated fragment “student) | $125.00,” which does not identify the charge [5]. Off-campus students are charged 6.63% NJ sales tax on parking fees; on-campus students are exempt [1]. The regular permit price is not clear in the provided fee text [5].

For questions, Public Safety: parkingpermits@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7432; include your Ramapo student ID number (R#) in an email [8, 12].

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/parking/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/costinfo/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/how-to-apply-for-a-parking-permit/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq-2/)

question: My RA wrote me up for a candle. what happens now? do i have to go to a hearing

body.answer:
A candle is a prohibited item, and Residence Life staff address prohibited-item violations. [9] The Office of Student Conduct receives incident reports from Residence Life staff and other sources. [18] Check your college email daily; conduct communications are sent there, and missing a message is not an excuse for missing a hearing or deadline. [21]

The pages don’t say that every candle write-up requires a hearing, so I can’t verify whether you personally have to attend one. If the Office schedules a hearing, the page describes it as an opportunity to talk about what happened; trying to avoid responsibility may lead to more severe sanctions. [5] Contact the Office of Student Conduct with questions about your case. [13, 21] You may have an advisor of your choosing, including an attorney, present, but the advisor may not speak during the hearing. [1]

The listed consequences depend on what violation is charged and whether it is a first or later offense. For “Activating a fire alarm due to a disregard of a published policy,” with candles as an example, the first violation is a $150 fine and fire-safety reflection assignment; the second is a $300 fine, disciplinary probation, and possible suspension or loss of housing privileges. [6] The sanctions page gives the same first- and second-violation amounts and lists possible relocation for the second violation. [4] These are for activating a fire alarm—not necessarily for possession of a candle alone. [4, 6]

Office of Student Conduct: studentconduct@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7869, C-212. [1, 21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/hearing/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/recommended-judicial-sanctions/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/frequently-asked-questions/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/fire-safety/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [18](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/frequently-asked-questions/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-affairs/student-communications/student-handbook-aug-22-2026/)

question: how do I get credit for my internship? I need to register for it but dont know where to start

body.answer:
Start with the Cahill Career Development Center. Co-op is an academic course, and you request permission to register. After you’re accepted for an internship: [1]
1. Select and meet with a co-op faculty advisor to determine your learning objectives and academic assignment. [1]
2. Request a “(co-op) Experience” on Handshake, then meet with your career advisor. [1]
3. Get “Registration Permission” from the Career Center. Permission lets you take the course; it is not registration. [1]
4. If choosing Pass/Fail, complete the appropriate form with Academic Advisement. If you are an international student on a J1 or other visa, get authorization from the international advisor and complete the appropriate paperwork. [1]
5. Register through “Self Service” on “My Ramapo.” [1]

Complete a Learning Agreement approved by your faculty advisor, career advisor, and employment supervisor. [9] An internship must provide meaningful work related to your major and/or career objective, building on classroom or academic experience. [3] Co-op is available in fall, spring, and summer. The published hour minimums are 120 hours in a semester for 2 credits or 240 hours for 4 credits. [2]

The pages differ on credits: section 2 lists 2- or 4-credit options; section 9 says each successfully completed co-op course is 4 credits. The pages also differ on orientation: section 4 requires first-time students to attend one orientation and all students to attend reflection; section 9 says students must attend both. [2][4][9]

Contact the Cahill Career Development Center: careercenter@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7444 (Main Office, C-209) or (201) 684-7675 (ASB Office, ASB-513). [1]

question: What do I need to do to move out of my dorm when I graduate? is there a checkout process and what happens if I'm late

body.answer:
Housing & Residence Life handles residence-hall check-out. Contact reslife@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7461; the checklist also says to contact your RA or Hall office before check-out. [1]

For spring end-of-year check-out:
1. Follow the [check-out checklist](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/check-out-checklist/). Remove trash and recyclables, personal items and property; leave the College refrigerator on at level 5; set the thermostat to auto, low, at 70°F; clean thoroughly; close blinds, lock windows, turn off lights, close the door, empty your campus mailbox, update correspondents with your new mailing address, and leave drawers open. [1]
2. Leave by the check-out deadline based on your last exam schedule. [1] The pages here don’t give your graduating term’s specific deadline; check with Housing & Residence Life.
3. Provide your own cart or dolly if needed; the College won’t provide moving equipment. Items left behind will be discarded, and fines may apply. [2] Final inspections happen after residents vacate; occupants should prepare the room, suite, or apartment together. Failed inspections or prohibited items may be billed. [9] The College is not responsible for belongings left behind. [9]

If you need to stay past the designated date and time, complete the [Check-Out Extension Request process](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/). Extensions won’t be granted for non-academic reasons, including unavailable/late transportation or off-campus employment; approved extensions don’t allow guests. [6] Not vacating as required may result in a $75 improper check-out fine. [2] The fines page says failure to follow posted check-out times is $75. [4] For excessive garbage, section 1 says fines start at $25 per bundle, while section 4 says $25 per bag; the pages differ. [1][4]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/check-out-checklist/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/spring-check-out/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/spring-check-out/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/spring-check-out/)

question: how can i see if I've met all my graduation requirements? is there a degree audit thing

body.answer:
Yes. The Registrar says students should review their degree audit and meet with their adviser to ensure they have met all graduation requirements [1]. The Center for Student Success says to access your degree evaluation: visit https://web.ramapo.edu/; click “Web for Students,” “Web Registration,” enter the Secure Area with your Ramapo login and password, then click “Student and Financial Aid,” “Student Records,” and “Degree Evaluation.” Select the current term and click enter; click “Generate New Evaluation,” select the circle next to your major and click “Generate Request,” select “detail requirements,” then click “Submit” [7].

The Provost’s page says that, as of March 2026, all continuing students use DegreeWorks as their degree audit tool, and links a guide, “How to Run a DegreeWorks Audit” [8, 10]. The pages differ on the audit tool: section 7 gives Degree Evaluation steps, while section 10 says continuing students use DegreeWorks. For graduation application, your degree audit must have all areas satisfied; make an appointment with your advisor to confirm readiness, and ask your advisor or convener about any needed audit adjustment before applying [6].

Questions about your audit: email degreeaudit@ramapo.edu [10]. Registrar: reg@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7695, D-224 [1].

question: what's my gpa right now and will I graduate with honors

body.answer:
I don’t have verified information about your current GPA or whether you’ll graduate with honors; those depend on your academic record. Ramapo calculates GPA after each term ends, using quality points divided by quality hours; only Ramapo courses count [4]. You can use the GPA calculator to estimate an anticipated GPA [1], or contact the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising) at success@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7441 [1].

Latin Honors are awarded automatically to undergraduate graduates based on cumulative GPA, including “R” grade credits: 3.500–3.699 cum laude, 3.700–3.849 magna cum laude, and 3.850–4.000 summa cum laude [6]. The catalog also says students must complete a minimum of 64 credits not including P grades at Ramapo College [5]; that section is specifically about the Spring 2020 emergency pass/fail option, a past term. Contact the Registrar at reg@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7695 [6].
